states.verdict: B's menu rises straight out of the bar it came from, centred over the three counts. The bar gets a #e1e1e1 hover pill so you can see what you clicked, and the menu is laid out on one label column. A's menu drops in off to the right, about 280 px away from the bar, as if it belonged to some other control. But B lies to you: a tick beside Hide Statistics while the numbers sit right under it is the kind of small untruth that makes a writer stop trusting the chrome. B still reads as the tighter, better-placed piece of interface. A's cleaner ticks don't make up for a menu that seems to come from nowhere.

states.verdict: A's foot is a row of pale grey words with nothing under it. Without a rule it reads as a stray caption, not a bar, and the '.md' on the title is file-manager clutter a writer doesn't need to see at the top of every draft. B puts the counts at the prose's own ink, closes the bar with a proper hairline, and names the document the way a writer thinks of it. B's selection band runs outside the text column, which is sloppy page-drawing, but the question here is the chrome, and there B is the finished one.
